subfield: Theoretical physics: quantum gravity, string theory and quantum field theory
motivation: Maldacena's 1997 conjecture that a strongly coupled gauge theory is exactly equivalent to a theory of quantum gravity in anti-de Sitter space, made precise by Witten and by Gubser, Klebanov and Polyakov through the field-operator dictionary, changed how physicists think about spacetime itself. Holography gave the first concrete, calculable realisation of the idea that gravity can emerge from quantum degrees of freedom without gravity, and it resolved in principle the black hole information paradox by showing that black hole evolution is unitary. Its tools now reach far beyond string theory: the shear viscosity bound tested at RHIC and the LHC in quark-gluon plasma, strange metals and quantum critical transport in condensed matter, and the link between entanglement and geometry that now joins quantum information and gravity research. Few ideas of the past thirty years have been taken up so widely across theoretical physics or have opened so many new ways of thinking.
